recipes.name: Moo Shu Pork
ingredients_raw: 1 pound pork tenderloin, cut into thin strips
2 tablespoons peeled and minced fresh ginger
1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus more if needed
16 frozen Chinese moo shu pancakes, thawed and warmed

steps.text: Place 2 tablespoons white wine, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 teaspoons cornstarch, and 1 teaspoon sesame oil into a non-reactive bowl; stir until smooth. Stir pork into marinade until thoroughly coated; refrigerate for 30 to 60 minutes.

Meanwhile, pour hot water over mushrooms in a small bowl; set aside to soften for 15 to 20 minutes. Drain mushrooms; pat dry, remove any hard stem pieces, and finely chop. Combine mushrooms, green onions, garlic, and ginger in a medium bowl; set aside.

Remove outer leaves from napa cabbage; tear green leafy portions from the central stalks of the leaves. Slice stalks into thin, 1-inch pieces. Finely chop green leafy portions; set aside the sliced stems and chopped leaves in separate bowls.
Whisk 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 3 tablespoons white wine, remaining 1/2 teaspoon cornstarch, sugar, and ground black pepper together in a small bowl until combined; set aside.
Heat oil and 1 teaspoon sesame oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add marinated pork; cook and stir until cooked through and edges have begun to brown, about 5 minutes. Transfer pork to a bowl.

Pour beaten eggs into the hot wok, adding more oil if needed; cook and stir until eggs are scrambled and firm, about 2 minutes. Stir in mushroom mixture; cook and stir for 1 to 2 minutes. Add napa cabbage stem pieces; cook and stir until hot but still crunchy, about 1 minute. Add chopped cabbage leaves and remaining 2 tablespoons white wine; cook and stir until hot, about 1 minute. Add cooked pork and reserved cornstarch mixture. Stir everything together until slightly thickened and hot, about 2 minutes.
Mix hoisin sauce, remaining 1 tablespoon soy sauce, and remaining 1 teaspoon sesame oil together in a small bowl until thoroughly combined.
To serve, spread about 1 tablespoon hoisin mixture over each pancake, top with about 1/2 cup pork mixture, and roll up.

raw_recipe.headline: Moo Shu Pork
raw_recipe.description: Moo shu pork, or mu shu, is an easy, delicious Chinese stir-fry of pork, mushrooms, ginger, and egg, served in Chinese pancakes with hoisin sauce.

review.reviewBody: I love mu shu and this really hit the spot for me. Yum!

this turned out really well. I made a few adjustments, using chow mein noodles in place of the pancakes, and only adding a little bit of hoisin sauce when I tossed the meat mix and noodles together. My only complaint is that it was a bit salty, so I may cut down on the soy sauce a bit.

I thought this recipe was great. I used rice spring roll wrappers and plum sauce. The wrappers and plum sauce are found at any Asian market or on Amazon, or other places online and very easy to find. I have to be gluten free so I make my own Amerasian food so I get a variety of all the good stuff, and this is good!

I've been craving mu shu pork for months because I haven't been able to go to my favorite Chinese restaurant. This tastes exactly like it, I'm so happy! My only note is to use low sodium soy sauce otherwise it may be a little salty

This makes a great, quick at home Asian dish that the family likes. Changes: I used pre-packaged slaw mix, leftover chicken or pork, any mushroom mostly for texture rather than flavor and flour wraps instead of pancakes. Don't skip the green onions and add extra ginger. Definitely spread the hoisin all over the wraps, as this is what gives the dish its flavor. If you like spice, add sriracha or cayenne powder.
This recipe turned out really well. I did substitute firm crumbled tofu for the eggs since eggs are crazy expensive right now and to lower the cholesterol level of the dish.

I might try it again adding matchstick carrots and pea pods, as well as strips of bamboo shoots and celery, oyster mushrooms, bean sprouts, and water chestnuts. It just needed more to it. The sauce was OK but a bit thick.
Great dish! I made it vegetarian by replacing the pork with tofu sliced in 1 inch strips and by not using the egg. Great recipe. Thank you.
I used what I had on hand, so I didn’t follow the recipe exactly. With that said, we loved it! I’ve been craving Asian flavors and this hit the spot! Will definitely be making this again.
I thought it was very good. I will make it again.

This was really tasty. However, another reviewer had suggested using spring roll wrappers as the pancakes which we tried and found they don't really work with a hot filling. We ended up just putting the mu shu on rice.
Loved this recipe! The hoisin sauce is a must. Loved putting this dish together. Not sure how anyone could consider this meal plain.
